speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify the timing: how many days old is your baby, and when did you first notice the yellowing? Also, has the baby been feeding well, or are there any signs of fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the weight gain is reassuring. Since the jaundice began after the first week, I need to know if she has had any dark urine or pale stools, and whether her mother is taking any medications or has blood type incompatibilities like O-negative or Rh-negative. REQUEST TEST: Total bilirubin level. REQUEST TEST: Direct bilirubin level.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Total Bilirubin: 16.1 mg/dL; Direct Bilirubin: 0.7 mg/dL

speaker: Doctor
text: The total bilirubin of 16.1 mg/dL with a normal direct fraction confirms significant unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia. Given the age of 14 days and the rising trend, have you noticed the stool color turning clay-colored or the urine becoming dark, which would suggest a biliary obstruction? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. I also have Exclusively breastfed, Brother died 3 months after liver surgery.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (Prolonged). The clinical picture of a well-growing 2-week-old with exclusively breastfed history and rising unconjugated bilirubin without signs of cholestasis (normal direct bilirubin, no clay stools) is most consistent with this benign condition, likely exacerbated by insufficient intake or suboptimal milk transfer in the early days. The family history of a sibling requiring liver surgery is noted but less likely to indicate a primary genetic liver disease given the current normal direct fraction.
